eyebrow: Averages hide the shape of the load
code:
# a VM idle at 2% for 23 hours, pegged at 95% for 1 hour
# daily batch job = averages out to ~12% CPU
#
# sizing off that 12% average would cause the batch job
# to miss its window or fall over
#
# p50  = typical interval, context only
# p95  = below this 95% of the time -- size against THIS
# p99  = catches rare but severe spikes
caption: p95 utilization, not the mean, is the standard right-sizing input.

eyebrow: Pulling p95 CPU in Log Analytics
code:
Perf
| where ObjectName == "Processor"
      and CounterName == "% Processor Time"
| where TimeGenerated > ago(28d)
| summarize p50 = percentile(CounterValue, 50),
            p95 = percentile(CounterValue, 95),
            p99 = percentile(CounterValue, 99)
          by Computer
| order by p95 desc
caption: 28 days captures weekly batch cycles and month-end spikes, not just a quiet Tuesday.

steps.label: p95 consistently under ~40%
steps.sub: downsize one or two tiers, keep real headroom

steps.label: p95 consistently above ~75-80%
steps.sub: undersized — a reliability problem before it's an incident

steps.label: Re-run the query monthly or quarterly
steps.sub: a one-time cleanup decays right back to where it started
